page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance architected on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 platform. Powered by AWS Graviton technology and managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity stands at 128 GB, giving a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is directly integrated on-instance through a 3800 GB local NVMe SSD, avoiding external network storage overhead for temporary files. Network connectivity delivers a 30 Gbps baseline throughput. No discrete graphics accelerator is included in this configuration.

Synthetic and application benchmarks highlight strong horizontal scalability across all 64 cores. Multi-core evaluations demonstrate upper-decile execution, led by Geekbench multi-core scores and Clang software compilation metrics. Memory subsystems achieve top-tier PassMark memory scores and sustained uncached read bandwidth exceeding 276 GB/sec. Data processing tests show robust throughput, with Redis recording over 100 million SET operations per second and static web serving surpassing 71 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics in stress-ng, compression, and Geekbench settle into the middle quartile, reflecting standard per-core execution speeds rather than ultra-high individual core clocks.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the dedicated 64-core arm64 architecture offers high execution density without thread-contention penalties common in symmetric multithreading environments. The bundled NVMe SSD volume removes the cost and latency overhead of provisioning high-IOPS external block volumes. Because memory is limited to 2 GB per core, workloads requiring deep in-memory datasets per thread may face constraints. The instance is optimally aligned with parallel CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed caching engines, high-concurrency web tiers, and batch ETL workloads that benefit from direct local NVMe access.

Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading, it provides 128 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration integrates 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 30 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core throughput, achieving top-tier ratings in Clang software compilation and Geekbench multi-core tests, paired with strong memory bandwidth and Redis operations exceeding 100 million transactions per second. While single-thread benchmarks reflect standard mid-range results, the system delivers high computational density and efficient parallel processing. The server is well matched for software build pipelines, high-throughput caching layers, batch data processing, and distributed database nodes requiring rapid local disk access.
